# Robot problem solving protocol v3

## Scope and tool use
Use only the supplied evidence and allowlisted harness functions within the stated budgets. Existing collection entry points are applicability information, not permission to invoke shell, files, network or hardware. Do not solve held-out cases or supply memorized repairs. Preserve safety, speed, recording requirements and independent native success criteria.

## Evidence-first sequence
1. Inspect the episode summary before selecting a repair. Separate task outcome, recording verification and causal diagnosis: a verified recording may document failure without identifying its cause. Report missing outcomes as null, not inferred success or failure.
2. Record task, source versions, initial state, action fingerprint, physical completion criteria, observed effects, earliest observed anomaly and final outcome. Separate FACTS, HYPOTHESES and UNKNOWN. Nonzero task error outside its relevant task phase is not automatically an anomaly; interpret metrics against existing criteria and phase expectations.
3. Retrieve at most five applicable memory records. Check task, failure signature, source/geometry versions, units, observation access and initial-state coverage. Read evidence references rather than whole histories. Previous retention failures do not establish retention failure in a new episode.
4. Treat sampled chronology as incomplete. Report the earliest supported anomaly or an uncertainty interval, not an invented onset. No observed retention loss does not establish a stable grasp: sliding and rotation can occur while contact persists. A late error or release snapshot does not identify the initiating cause.

## Targeted contact and state inspection
Request an inspection only when its result could distinguish stated hypotheses. Choose a relevant frame or transition, explain the observable distinction sought, and respect the remaining budget. Prefer available adjacent-state evidence around a suspected transition over repeatedly inspecting a terminal state. Do not assume an unavailable tool or observation exists.

A recorded contact pair establishes neither active constraint nor gripping force. Distinguish recorded pairs, solver-active constraints and reconstructed solver forces. For each inspection, report state source, force source, frame/time, units, model/asset provenance and reconstruction limits. A forward solve on restored integration state is Simulation-only evidence, not a real force measurement, historical force trace or executed intervention. Zero simulation steps do not constitute a trial.

Check contact activation, exclusion, margin, collision representation and overrides before interpreting contact geometry. Invisible collision geoms or convex hulls need not match visible surfaces. Contact-point-to-visible-mesh distance is not a silhouette gap or full surface separation; it alone establishes neither a geometry defect nor a correction. Current mesh hashes do not recover unrecorded historical asset identity.

Snapshot applied-force fields describe that snapshot only. They cannot exclude earlier forces, direct state edits, teleports or callbacks. Keep historical provenance UNKNOWN unless independently recorded. Simulator actuator force and gripper motor feedback are not measured six-axis force/torque. Do not convert actuator units into real motor torque without an identified mapping. This robot has no six-axis force/torque sensor; real visual evidence is RGB only.

## Hypotheses and bounded experiments
Propose at most three causes, each with supporting evidence, unresolved alternatives and a falsifiable observable prediction. An uncertainty statement is not itself a causal hypothesis. Compare proposed actions with negative experiences; do not repeat a contradicted repair under matching conditions without new evidence.

Before a repair trial, specify applicability, one changed variable, justified bounds, unchanged controls, expected discriminating observation, existing success checks and budget. Do not derive repair values from a terminal snapshot alone. If a change occurs after the earliest observed anomaly, explain how it addresses the hypothesized cause rather than merely masking the outcome. Never tune friction, remove collisions, alter speed or weaken evaluators to obtain a pass.

Prefer reversible, bounded simulation probes when available evidence supports them. Root-cause uncertainty need not prevent a discriminating observation, but it does not justify an arbitrary parameter sweep. If no supported probe is available within the tools and budget, stop with STOPPED_UNKNOWN, retain the active configuration and list the missing evidence needed to proceed. A proposal is not execution or calibration.

## Validation and reporting
Save inputs, config/source hashes, evidence references, disclosed privileged fields, actual planner kind, model invocation, metrics, failures and exceptions through authorized interfaces. Missing measurements are null. Keep inference time, simulated time, actual robot time and interventions separate.

Validate a supported change against the original condition and predeclared independent initial states without using held-out answers to choose repairs. Promote only within demonstrated applicability; record regressions and restore the prior active version on failure. Preserve existing complete-Episode recording and replay verification for successes and failures; headless trials and observation sequences are not complete successful Episodes.

Simulation privileged state must be labeled Simulation-only. Give comparison groups equivalent observation access or separate access effects from method effects. Calibration requires bounded parameters, real measured targets and withheld real validation; visual fit or software FK consistency alone is insufficient. SIMULATION_VERIFIED never authorizes hardware. Real movement still requires fresh explicit human permission, validated simulation and unchanged existing safety checks. Do not claim real verification, general competence or cost reduction from this evidence.
